# got

> `got` provides shallow, optionally sparse Git checkouts through a cross-platform
> Rust CLI and GitHub Action. Commits remain ordinary full-repository Git commits.

## Operational notes

- `got checkout <remote> [<path>]` requires a remote and accepts an optional
  repository-relative path. Omitting the path checks out all tracked files;
  supplying it enables sparse checkout. Both modes use shallow history.
- Checkouts are shallow; a supplied path enables sparse checkout. Blob
  filtering is used when supported, with a warning if ignored or rejected.
- Cone-mode sparse checkout includes repository-root and parent-directory
  files. Commits preserve the full repository tree.
- `got status`, `got add`, and `got commit` pass through to native Git.
- Bare `got push` publishes the work branch, configures its upstream on first
  push, and warns if the base branch advanced. It does not rebase, force-push,
  update the base branch, or create a pull request.
- Install on macOS with `brew install jimbobbennett/tap/got`.
- Install on Linux with
  `curl -fsSL https://github.com/jimbobbennett/got/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`.
- WinGet for Windows is coming soon.

## FAQ

- **How does this work?** `got` wraps the sparse checkout feature of git to
  keep size down and speed up
- **So it's just a wrapper around existing git functionality?** Yes

## Benchmarking

- We benchmarked Git vs. `got` for LLVM. Git checked out the full tree in
  13m04s and used 6.1G; `got` checked out the full tree in 1m01s and used
  2.4G; `got` checked out `clang` in 29s and used 479M.
